author: worker-7
scope: Representative static source traces in four already-acquired repositories. No upstream import, build, installer, server, model or get-env execution.
spanEncoding: Inclusive 1-based source lines; concatenate original UTF-8 line bytes including their existing LF terminators, without adding a final newline.

baseline.addendumHeading: ## Addendum — 2026-09-13: four representative protocol and adapter traces

opencode.inspectionDepth: Catalog discovery/cache/naming, ordinary MCP tool wrapping, permission decision, selected provider-schema lowering and AI SDK repair callback. Native/code-mode/provider backend paths are not fully audited.

langchain.inspectionDepth: Tool discovery/conversion, default and explicit session lifetimes, error/content conversion and stdio/session routing. Python MCP SDK and LangChain core dependencies are not deconstructed by these adapter spans.

sdk.inspectionDepth: Modular upstream client/server stdio, framing and selected shared-protocol request/cancellation/close paths. This is distinct from the installed monolithic SDK 1.30.0.

servers.inspectionDepth: Filesystem path validation, roots, selected read/write handlers and everything stdio/default get-env registration. Other reference servers and complete concurrent filesystem safety are not audited.

evidence.observation: Tolerant listing omits outputSchema; pagination rejects duplicate cursors and caps at 1000 pages; defs converts listing failure to no result.

Tool schema is forced to object with properties and additionalProperties=false; dispatch forwards args with progress-reset timeout and abort signal; isError throws; structured-only success gains text content.
Tool naming sanitizes characters; tools/list retries selected output-schema validation errors through the tolerant schema.
Enabled connections discover advertised tools; missing discovery fails and closes the connected client.
Close removes cached client/tool state; successful list-change refresh replaces definitions, while a failed refresh returns without replacing them.
Only connected cached catalogs are exposed; each definition is assigned into a record keyed by the sanitized server/tool name.
Execution context carries abort/session/call identity and merges agent/session permission rules for ask.
Ordinary MCP tools receive provider schema transformation; plugin-before runs, permission ask precedes MCP execute, plugin-after runs, then content/attachments and truncation are projected.
Last matching wildcard rule wins with ask fallback; deny rejects, allow proceeds, and ask awaits a deferred permission response.

Selected JSON-schema keywords survive OpenAI lowering; boolean schemas become string schemas, an empty schema remains empty, and lowering is gated on the exact OpenAI/Azure SDK package route; Moonshot has a separate branch.
AI SDK streamText receives the prepared tools and abort signal; repair only corrects matching lowercase tool names or redirects to invalid with diagnostic JSON.
Tool listing follows cursors, treats a false cursor as completion and caps at 1000 iterations.
Discovery without a supplied session initializes a temporary session, lists tools, exits it, and converts tools with the original session=None plus connection configuration.

Calls without a supplied session open/initialize a new session; explicit sessions are reused. Call exceptions are re-raised outside temporary context teardown. Tool inputSchema becomes StructuredTool args_schema; annotations are metadata.
A dedicated ToolException subclass carries MCP execution-error content; its handler preserves content or supplies an empty-error placeholder, and rethrows unrelated ToolException instances.

Audio and unknown content raise conversion errors; content conversion precedes isError processing. Successful structuredContent becomes a separate artifact; interceptor ToolMessage/Command results can bypass ordinary conversion.
Configured interceptors wrap dispatch in order, with the first interceptor outermost.
Explicit client.session yields inside a live initialized context; get_tools passes no session and connection configuration, including concurrent discovery across servers.
Braced environment references expand from os.environ; unknown references remain literal and bare dollar syntax is not expanded.

Configured environment values are expanded, then passed with command/args/cwd/encoding to Python MCP stdio_client and ClientSession context managers; Python SDK internals remain a dependency boundary.
Session routing validates transport presence and required command/args or URL fields, wires callbacks and selects the configured transport.
The stdio client merges filtered default environment with configured environment, spawns without a shell, wires stdout/errors/close and optionally pipes stderr.

Private probe disposal awaits exit and destroys pipe handles; public close ends stdin then escalates child signals after two-second races, without awaiting final SIGKILL completion; sends respect write backpressure.
Server transport reads buffered messages, reports errors, removes its listeners and conditionally pauses stdin on close; send rejects closed/error states and handles drain.
A ten-MiB default buffer cap applies before parsing; newline frames decode UTF-8, non-JSON syntax-error lines are skipped, valid-JSON schema failures surface, and writes append a newline.
Cancellation aborts the matching request-handler controller; progress timeout reset can check an optional maximum total timeout.
Protocol connect dispatches transport messages; close settles pending responses with ConnectionClosed, clears timers and aborts active request-handler controllers.
Each handler receives a cancellation signal; replies are suppressed after abort; encoding/handler failures map to protocol error responses and handler state is removed.

Outbound stdio cancellation sends a best-effort notification except for initialize; modern per-request HTTP streams use a different branch. Local promises reject, returned results are validated, and per-request listeners/maps/timers are cleaned.
The acquired upstream client package identifies itself as @modelcontextprotocol/client 2.0.0 with modular exports, not the installed @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.0 artifact.

Relative resolution uses allowed directories; validation checks lexical and realpath containment, rejects Windows drive syntax on POSIX, and resolves missing/Unicode-equivalent path components with ambiguity checks.

New files use exclusive creation; existing targets use a random sibling temporary file then rename, with cleanup and best-effort permission restoration. No fsync or expected-content CAS appears in this helper.
Command-line roots are normalized, resolved and filtered for accessible directories before setting the library's allowed directories.

read_multiple_files embeds each read failure in returned content without setting top-level isError; write_file validates a path then writes and reports success text with destructive/idempotent annotations.

Nonempty validated client roots replace allowed directories; empty/invalid roots retain the old set. Startup and roots/list_changed fetch client roots; no intersection with the original CLI roots appears here.
Roots are decoded, resolved and checked for directory existence; invalid entries are skipped. This helper has no original-root authorization ceiling.
Containment rejects empty/NUL/type errors and checks equality or a directory-separator boundary, with root/drive handling.
Path normalization has OS-specific branches and trims surrounding whitespace/quotes; tilde expansion uses the server process home.
The filesystem package declares @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.30.0 and a build prepare script; this manifest is not proof of a resolved dependency set and no script was run.
Everything selects stdio by default and dynamically imports only the requested transport.
The stdio entrypoint creates and connects the server; its explicit SIGINT handler closes, cleans up and exits.
The factory installs default tools before initialization and capability-conditional tools afterward, with in-memory task storage and delayed root synchronization.
get-env is included in unconditional registerTools, separately from capability-conditional registrations.
get-env returns JSON.stringify(process.env) as text with no value filtering in this callback, despite readOnly/non-destructive/idempotent/closed-world annotations.

contextEvidence.observation: Direct byte inspection independently confirms the installed default-environment merge. Excluded from acquired-repository coverage counts.

Prime-owned current code blanks SDK inherited keys, restores PATH plus envAllow, drains stderr and rejects duplicate catalogs/cursors. This is local source observation, not this worker's runtime verification.

Four prime-owned synthetic controls inspect environment key presence, explicit allowlisting, stderr drainage and duplicate/cursor handling. Prime reported four passes; this slice reads the test source and does not rerun or claim authorship of that result.

requirements.requirement: Record original, client-transformed and provider-sent schema identities and validate actual arguments at the host boundary; never infer provider schema from a model's name.
requirements.counterexample: Present nested {}, boolean false, a numeric minimum and a required object input through the actual selected provider route; reject wrong-type arguments and record each transformation before assigning blame.

requirements.requirement: Bind dispatch to an unambiguous, versioned catalog; reject name collisions and detect stale discovery before effects.
requirements.counterexample: Use two distinct server/tool names that normalize to the same key, a repeated cursor, and a tool schema changed after discovery; require explicit rejection or a new qualified catalog.

requirements.requirement: Keep capability visibility, permission decisions and exact effect admission distinct; trusted interceptors must not silently weaken the host contract.
requirements.counterexample: Authorize one harmless tool call, change its consequential arguments or interceptor routing, and require a fresh host decision where the deployment contract binds authorization to those arguments.

requirements.requirement: Declare whether tools share a live session, a subprocess or durable server state; execute stateful sequences within the required lifetime.
requirements.counterexample: Run a synthetic reserve/commit pair whose reservation lives only in server memory; compare default per-call sessions with an explicitly retained session and reject any claim of implicit state continuity.

requirements.requirement: Preserve execution failure, transport failure, conversion failure and per-item partial failure as distinct outcomes; independent task checks must inspect required outputs.
requirements.counterexample: Return isError text, unsupported audio, a disconnected session and a mixed-success multi-file response; none may become task success merely because a wrapper returned content.

requirements.requirement: Enforce the effective child environment after adapter/default merging and configuration interpolation; separate key blanking from OS sandbox authority.
requirements.counterexample: In a synthetic child only, seed harmless allowed and denied markers plus default inherited keys, then assert exact nonempty key names without returning real host values.
requirements.status: proposed-not-run; related prime-owned installed-SDK controls are separately identified

requirements.requirement: Use a host total deadline and explicit cancellation/effect reconciliation; request rejection, server signal and process-tree termination are different receipts.
requirements.counterexample: Use a synthetic operation that ignores its request signal, emits progress indefinitely, or leaves a pipe-holding helper; verify bounded host settlement separately from actual cessation and committed effects.

requirements.requirement: Treat stdout framing and bounded buffers as part of the transport contract, drain stderr, and expose protocol errors without inventing valid responses.
requirements.counterexample: Send split UTF-8 frames, non-JSON lines, valid-JSON invalid envelopes, an over-limit chunk and large synthetic stderr; verify the intended adapter-specific behavior and timeout result.

requirements.requirement: Declare who may replace filesystem roots and how revocation works; deployments needing a fixed ceiling must intersect dynamic roots with that host-owned ceiling.
requirements.counterexample: Advertise a second synthetic directory outside initial CLI roots, then publish an empty roots list; distinguish replacement from intersection and explicit revocation from retention.

requirements.requirement: Separate lexical/canonical path checks, leaf replacement, ancestor-race protection, durability and expected-content conflict checks.
requirements.counterexample: In an isolated fake directory tree, try a sibling-prefix path, POSIX Windows-drive input, ambiguous Unicode names, a changed ancestor between validation and write, and a concurrent content change; assess each promised property independently.

requirements.requirement: Review what data a capability discloses in addition to its effect annotations; do not automatically admit debug tools from an everything catalog.
requirements.counterexample: Offer a read-only annotated synthetic environment-dump tool whose output contains a harmless secret marker; require host selection/redaction rules independently of readOnlyHint.

requirements.requirement: Pin the actually installed transport and its dependency closure separately from source research; require version-specific evidence before transferring guarantees.
requirements.counterexample: Change only the installed SDK build or select a modular export with different framing/disposal code; prior clone hashes and prior test receipts must not qualify the replacement.

limitations: Source observations and logically derived counterexamples are not executed upstream tests or security exploit reproductions.
